sentences.text: Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta Ga appearing on behalf of Advocate General.
Heard on I.A No.1946/2025, which is second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for grant of suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant - Vikram Singh.
Appellant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 24.08.2022.

2. The appellant has been convicted u/S 376 (2), 363, 366 of IPC alongwith 6(1) (2)/5(l) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo RI for 03 years with fine of Rs.2500/-, RI for 05 years with fine of Rs.2500/-, RI for 20 years with fine of Rs.25,000/-, respectively with usual default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Counsel for the appellant argued that as per the prosecution story, a report was lodged by father of the prosecutrix alleging that her daughter was missing.
It is alleged against the appellant that he had abducted the minor girl and committed rape with her on various occasions.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that as per the statements of the the prosecutrix, she was a consenting party and she herself had gone with the appellant to different places and was recovered after 10 days.
The prosecution has failed to prove the source on the basis of which the age of the prosecutrix was recorded in the scholar register.
Appellant has already remained in jail for more than five years and six months.
Final hearing of the appeal is likely to take sufficient time.

Under these circumstances, it is prayed that jail sentence of the appellant be suspended.
5.
Per contra, counsel for the State has opposed the prayer by submitting that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the testimony of the prosecutrix it appears that she was a consenting party.
The prosecution has failed to prove that on what source the age of the prosecutrix was recorded in the scholar registrar.

In the case of Tijubai @
Omvati Bai and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2025(1) MPLJ (Cri.)75, it has been held that if the prosecution does not prove the source of date of birth recorded in scholar register and the same is recorded on the guess, the same cannot be the basis for conviction.

sentences.text: 7. Considering the same, the present application is allowed.

The jail sentence of appellant Sheikh Munir is suspended upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 11.11.2025 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Registry.
8. With the aforesaid, I.A No.1946/2025 is allowed and disposed of.
